newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Landsbergis party leads in Lithuania poll count.
newsitem.headline: Landsbergis party leads in Lithuania poll count.

text.p: The party of Lithuania's independence leader Vytautas Landsbergis took the lead early on Monday as results came in from the second round of the Baltic state's parliamentary elections.
Preliminary results from 37 of the 65 parliamentary seats showed that Landsbergis' Homeland Union was leading in 20 of them. His party won 35 seats in the 141-seat parliament in the first round.

Landsbergis, a short and stocky former music professor, led Lithuania's struggle to quit the former Soviet Union in 1990-91 but lost 1992 elections to the former communists of the Lithuanian Democratic Labour Party (LDLP).
The Christian Democrats, with whom the Homeland Union has promised to form a coalition, were leading in four of the 37 seats counted while the LDLP was ahead in just two.
The election marks Landsbergis' political comeback and is sweet revenge over his ex-communist rivals.

In power, the Homeland Union is expected to pursue Lithuania's path of integration with the European Union (EU) and NATO. Its economic policy has come under scrutiny as it wants to unpeg the litas currency from the dollar, worrying some foreign investors.
